clue.text: In my own country I may have baffled rural peasant!

definitions.text: In my own country I may have baffled rural peasant!

parts.note: the speaker is French, and in France the word for I is je

indicators.note: baffled suggests the letters of the following words are confused into a new order

explanation.surface: A French intellectual boasts that at home he could bewilder a simple country labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is spoken by the philosopher himself, a Frenchman, so 'I' in his own country is French; the whole sentence also describes how his dense ideas might puzzle a peasant.
explanation.definitionFit: The French existentialist philosopher, whose abstruse writing could easily perplex an ordinary farm worker in his homeland.

clue.text: Entertaining lady — see me mixing with atheists, getting among believers

indicators.note: getting among says the jumble goes inside the word for believers

parts.note: Jews are believers in Judaism

indicators.note: mixing with says the letters of me and atheists are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a performer while I mingle with unbelievers who end up in a congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is only a link. Jessie Matthews was a British stage and film star of the 1930s, famous for musicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Jessie Matthews was a celebrated British singer, dancer and actress, so a female entertainer.

clue.text: Different labels giving a lassie a different look

indicators.note: giving the words a different look means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Changing a girl's appearance earns her new names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a different look' rearranges A LASSIE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliases are assumed names, so alternative labels a person goes by.

clue.text: Legacy from which one gets a cut — 25 quid, about

indicators.note: about means the slang sum goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
a trim is a cut, as at the barber's

explanation.surface: An inheritance is described as something one takes a share of, worth a modest sum.
explanation.walkthrough: A pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds; 'from which one gets' is only a link describing what a legacy is.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrimony is property inherited from one's father or ancestors, a synonym for an inheritance.

clue.text: Upset serviceman loses leader before victory

indicators.note: loses leader means the first letter is dropped from the word for the serviceman

parts.note: a gunner is a soldier in the artillery
VE stands for victory in Europe, as in VE Day

explanation.surface: A soldier is distressed after losing his commanding officer just before the battle is won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses leader' cuts G from GUNNER to leave UNNER; VE is victory in Europe, as in VE Day, 8 May 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: To unnerve someone is to upset their composure, a synonym used here as a verb.

clue.text: Actress making final appearance that's no good

indicators.note: no good means the letter G, for good, is removed

parts.note: a swan song is a performer's last appearance

explanation.surface: A performer gives a farewell show that turns out to be a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's no good' takes G (good) out of SWANSONG. Gloria Swanson was the silent-film star of Sunset Boulevard.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloria Swanson was an American screen actress, famous for Sunset Boulevard.

clue.text: A gentleman getting up to accommodate a foreign lady

indicators.note: to accommodate means the reversed piece takes the next letter inside it
in a down clue getting up means the pieces read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight or a polite address to a gentleman

explanation.surface: A man rises from his seat to make room for a visiting woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns A SIR into RISA, and 'to accommodate' puts the second A inside it. Raisa is a Russian name, borne by Raisa Gorbachev.
explanation.definitionFit: Raisa is a Russian woman's name, so a lady from abroad for a British solver.

clue.text: Legislation to control activity instigated by letters

definitions.text: Legislation to control activity instigated by letters

parts.words: Legislation to control activity instigated by letters
parts.note: letters here are people who let property, landlords; the activity they set off is charging tenants money, and a law curbs it

explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' is not alphabet letters but people who let out rooms or houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute regulating what landlords may charge tenants for housing.

clue.text: A name — name in certain rime, possibly

definitions.text: A name — name in certain rime, possibly

parts.note: N again abbreviates name

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation sits inside the rearranged letters
possibly suggests the letters of certain rime could be rearranged

parts.note: N again abbreviates name

explanation.surface: A title is said to belong to a particular old poem.
explanation.walkthrough: A + N, then 'possibly' rearranges CERTAIN RIME and 'in' puts the second N inside to make CIENTMARINER. The whole clue also says this is the name in Coleridge's poem The Rime of the Ancient Mariner.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Coleridge's poem The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, an old seafarer.

clue.text: Boy with inclination to eat food from Cambridgeshire?

indicators.note: to eat means the boy takes the slope inside him

parts.note: a son is a boy
a tilt is a slope or inclination

explanation.surface: A lad who leans towards eating local produce.
explanation.walkthrough: The cheese takes its name from the village of Stilton, historically in Huntingdonshire, now Cambridgeshire, where it was sold; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton cheese is named after a village in Cambridgeshire where it was once marketed.

clue.text: A time I get lost in navigation around foreign town

indicators.note: get lost in means those letters are removed from the following word
around signals the remaining letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller admits losing time and getting lost while finding the way abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get lost in' removes A, T (time) and I from NAVIGATION, leaving NVGAION, and 'around' rearranges those into the French city of the popes.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon is a city in southern France, so a town abroad for a British solver.

clue.text: Immigrant is looking both ways across middle of sea

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: across means the pair of words goes round the next piece
looking both ways means the word is read forwards and then backwards
middle of picks the central letter of sea

explanation.surface: A newcomer arrives by sea, checking in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking both ways' gives IS forwards and SI backwards, and 'across' puts them round E, the middle of 'sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: Issei is a Japanese term for a first-generation emigrant, especially to the Americas.

clue.text: Old emperor in overlapping desert expedition

indicators.note: overlapping means the two words are not simply placed end to end but cross over where they meet

parts.note: to rat is to desert one's side
a safari is an expedition, often in Africa

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler sets out on a long trek across the sands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlapping' means the two words are not set end to end: the first letter of the expedition crosses into the desertion word, ahead of its final letter. 'Desert' tempts as a noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ras Tafari was the name of Haile Selassie, Emperor of Ethiopia, before his coronation.

clue.text: Removing Head of State after revolution, rule badly

indicators.note: after revolution means the letters are turned about into a new order
head of picks the first letter of State

explanation.surface: After an uprising deposes the president, the new regime governs poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' gives S from State, and 'after revolution' rearranges REMOVING + S. 'Removing' looks like part of the story but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To misgovern is to administer a country incompetently, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Staff try to increase score without making declaration

definitions.meaning: a staff or stick, such as a conductor's or relay runner's

definitions.text: try to increase score without making declaration
definitions.meaning: in cricket, a side that carries on batting rather than declaring its innings closed

explanation.surface: Employees try to boost the company's numbers without announcing anything.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a captain can declare, ending the innings early; to bat on is to keep scoring instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick or staff, and to bat on is to keep batting in cricket.

clue.text: Part of the business not allowed to broaden

parts.note: a branch is a local office or division of a company
out means not permitted, as in that's out

explanation.surface: A division of the firm is forbidden to expand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To branch out is to extend one's activities into new areas, so to widen their scope.

clue.text: Behind the marble facade is city brownish?

indicators.note: behind means the city comes after the marble

parts.note: a taw is a playing marble, especially the large shooter
NY is the abbreviation for New York City

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the city hidden behind a marble frontage is brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ... facade' says the marble is the front part of the word, with the city behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawny is an orange-brown or yellowish-brown colour, as of a lion's coat.

clue.text: Arrow I shot — before the start of rifles?

definitions.text: Arrow I shot — before the start of rifles?

indicators.note: shot suggests the letters are fired off into a new arrangement
the start of picks the first letter of rifles

explanation.surface: An archer explains that he fired arrows in the days before guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is a link. The whole clue pictures a fighter from the age of bows, the era before firearms.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter who shot arrows in the era before firearms existed.

clue.text: To the advantage of country, sergeant-major shows obsession with correct procedure

parts.note: for means in favour of, to the advantage of
Mali is a country in West Africa
SM is the military abbreviation for sergeant-major

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant serving his nation is fixated on doing everything by the book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Formalism is strict adherence to prescribed forms and rules, often excessively.

clue.text: Wide-angled like lens or codpiece?

definitions.meaning: describing a very wide-angle camera lens giving a curved image
read as a piece of a cod, an organ of the fish

explanation.surface: A tailor asks whether a wide-angled lens resembles a codpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'codpiece' is a Tudor garment in the surface but splits as cod (a fish) + piece (a part).
explanation.definitionFit: A fish-eye lens is an extreme wide-angle lens, and a cod's eye is literally a part of a fish.

clue.text: Get hot and bothered about a commie cleric once

indicators.note: about means the word for flushing goes round the letter A

parts.note: to redden is to flush with embarrassment or anger

explanation.surface: A communist priest gets flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside REDDEN. The Red Dean was Hewlett Johnson, Dean of Canterbury, known for his pro-Soviet views.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewlett Johnson, Dean of Canterbury, was nicknamed the Red Dean for his communist sympathies.

clue.text: Arrived before five? Almost three hours later! That's Rail for you!

parts.note: in means arrived, as in the train is in
V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: three hours after five o'clock is eight

explanation.surface: A passenger complains that a train due before five came in nearly three hours late, typical of the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: Three hours after five o'clock is eight. 'Rail' looks like the railway, encouraged by the train-delay surface, but is the verb meaning to complain bitterly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest angrily, and to inveigh is to speak bitterly against something.

clue.text: Astute as one is at bridge with viewers each side

definitions.meaning: shrewd and unsentimental in a practical way

definitions.text: as one is at bridge with viewers each side
definitions.meaning: the bridge is that of the nose, which is bony and firm there, with the eyes on either side

explanation.surface: A shrewd card player sits at the bridge table with spectators on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game, but it is the bridge of the nose, with the eyes as viewers either side; the nose is hard there.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-nosed means tough-minded and shrewd, realistic in business or negotiation.

clue.text: Just one of the hacks becoming famous?

definitions.meaning: a hack is a journalist; an ordinary one is not the editor

explanation.walkthrough: Split as NOT ED: not the editor (ED), just an ordinary reporter. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known or renowned, a synonym for famous.

clue.text: Cold? Not under blanket!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
over is the opposite of under

explanation.surface: Someone feeling chilly complains about not being under the bedclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blanket' looks like the bedding but is a noun for a covering of any kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A blanket is a covering layer, as in a blanket of snow, so a cover.

clue.text: Game allowed to be endless — has the ref lost it?

parts.note: whist is a card game

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: A football match is allowed to run on and on because the referee may have mislaid something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost it' tempts as losing one's temper; here the referee has mislaid the object he blows to stop play.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee stops play by blowing a whistle, so a match runs on if he has mislaid it.

clue.text: Someone who used to live in the USSR won't want son in a public school

definitions.note: describes a pupil who is at a particular school, a person rather than a place

indicators.note: won't want means the letter for son is left out

parts.words: Someone who used to live in the USSR
parts.note: Estonia was a Soviet republic, so an Estonian lived in the USSR

explanation.surface: A former Soviet citizen does not wish to send his boy to a posh British school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't want' drops S (son) from ESTONIAN. A British public school is a fee-paying private school; Eton is the most famous.
explanation.definitionFit: An Etonian is a pupil at Eton College, the famous English fee-paying school.

clue.text: Carl's going out with the dancer — she's very young and he's this?

definitions.text: she's very young and he's this?

indicators.note: going out with suggests the letters are rearranged as Carl is dating

parts.note: Carl's stands for Carl is, so its S counts

explanation.surface: Carl is dating a dancer who is very young, so people call him something unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out with' rearranges CARLS + THE DANCER into the answer; here 'Carl's' means Carl is, so its S is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradle-snatcher is someone who dates a much younger partner.
